One published approval and two competing selectors, plus a separate one-request retirement projection. Callback completion/failure and storage settlement are nondeterministic.
Role authorization, option validation, multiple pending approvals, durable recovery of task rows and process restart are outside these projections.

Stopping an already-pending request retains its durable task row. Callback failure retains the row but removes its in-memory callback. Unavailable callbacks fail closed; durable function reconstruction and retries remain unsupported.
Retirement assumes admitted callbacks settle and do not await their own service unload or stop. Independent instances running concurrently and reentrant lifecycle calls remain separate obligations.
Creation failure is checked before a successful commit. Unknown commit acknowledgements and external database mutation are outside these projections.

Two additional finite cases cover a single persisted required-callback task (sync or async) or callback-free async task, one runtime restart and same-name worker registration. Mixed callback shapes, legacy/externally changed metadata and startup deadline reconstruction remain open.

ChoiceApprovalCancellation separately models receipt-bearing cancellation. Core real SQLite checks cover delete acknowledgement before settlement, exclusive callback-free ownership, failure retry with the original deadline and concurrent stop success/failure. Legacy orphan cleanup has no cancellation receipt. A real committed-delete/lost-acknowledgement case also verifies that a missing task cannot produce a successful timeout callback receipt; unknown storage acknowledgement remains outside the finite model.
Two embedding calls and three probes across named, plain and wide providers. The original abstraction excludes disabled-generation and background re-embedding progress.

One queued item or one batch of two. The batch inference result supplies both items. The batch settles its writes and observers in order before any failed item falls back to a single request. Each item has at most two single attempts in this projection.

The adapter atomically compares the admitted source with one possible edit. The confirmed result is a stored vector or a stale-source refusal. A modeled write rejection occurs before commit. Diagnostic logging and completion publication may fail after the result, and neither starts another attempt.

Real AgentRuntime, repeat worker and PGlite cases verify stored vector readback, exact stale-source refusal, preservation of each batch item, and retry after a known uncommitted write rejection. Inference is a local fixture and diagnostic failures are controlled at their caller boundaries.

Independent batches, source reversion, lost storage acknowledgement, provider durability, task shutdown and individual event subscribers remain outside this projection. The fairness assumption does not guarantee successful inference, storage or observation.
